book_question: What is the Grace, really? (Book II; Darrow fights on his feet but cannot run: every fight held, not chased)

chapter.question: Who is the one rider on the long-legged horse, and can a man who cannot run hold a frozen weir against the finest footwork in the Lowmarch?

slots.plan: The first day on the road out of Coldmere (whichever road he chose at the fork; if the choice is still open, the scene stays on the first miles that both roads share, the dawn bell behind them over the water). At the noon halt Maelis reads the Knots, a week since the last Reading, with the company a little way off and pretending not to listen; then she takes his right hand and tells him plainly that the two last fingers will not come back whole: the frost from the kennel grate has left them slow and half-numb for good, a different grip on a sword from now on (ledger c04.12b, a fate: never the knee, never mended, never a lecture). He tries the grip on the stick, then on the oilcloth sword, and says what he thinks of it; Hollis, who fights from a chair, has an opinion. The road goes on.
slots.turn: Darrow learns what the frost took for good and finds the grip that is left to him; the company learns he can be told a hard thing and keep walking.

slots.plan: A rider on a long-legged horse on the skyline behind them at dusk, alone, not closing (thread 23: the horse shod for speed). Rae makes the road lie: she shifts the load and runs the cart twice over the soft ground at a crossing so that two carts' tracks go out of one, one set away up a side lane, then takes the real road; Wren counts the lie and approves of it. At the camp Hollis keeps his word from the Coldmere well: the second lesson, over the wall (Overwall), stones lobbed over the field wall into a hat on the far side, where the wall gives the mark no cover (callback c05.9a fires here). Darrow is cold and his hands are stupid and he puts the fourth stone in the hat.
slots.turn: The company learns it is hunted by one rider, not a column, and that a carter can make a road lie; Darrow learns the throw that goes over what stands between him and the mark.

invite.want: to teach the second throw he promised at Coldmere's well, while the Captain is cold and wants something to do with his hands
invite.if_ignored: he lobs stones over the wall alone until the light goes, and says nothing about it
invite.why_now: he said tomorrow, over the wall, at the well three days ago, and tonight's camp has a wall

slots.plan: The road's people, on the mill tracks: the tracks' inn in the hill country, where a drover tells the taproom that a rider on a long-legged horse stood a round and asked after a captain with a stick, and paid in good coin. A family that fled a river farm up the side lanes rather than east with the levy is in the inn yard with a lame ox and asks the company for the loan of Hob to the next village. The company is spoken of by strangers for the first time as a thing on the road, and a stranger asks something of it. Ends on the small choice.
slots.turn: Darrow finds the company has become a thing people on the road ask things of, and decides what it owes a stranger; the rider is confirmed as one who asks politely and pays well.

micro.ask: A family driven off their farm asks the company for help on the road, which will cost it a day with a rider behind it. What does Darrow do?
options: Give them the day: the company walks at their pace to the next safe place.
Give them bread and a word on the road ahead, and keep the company's own pace.
Ask Rae what the road's custom is, and do that.

slots.plan: The rider is seen plainly for the first time: a woman, slight, on the far side of a frozen water-meadow at noon, sitting a long-legged horse as still as a post, close enough to count the buttons on her coat and not closing. She watches the company a long while. Darrow's first move is the old one: toward her, across the meadow, alone, before anyone has said a word; whether he goes on is his, on the page, and what it costs him with the company follows from it. The company says its piece: Hollis names what she is by how she sits ('that's a duelist; look at her hands'); Maelis says the obvious thing, that a hunter who could have closed and did not is waiting for something; Rae keeps the oxen standing; Wren stops counting, which is how the company knows she is frightened; Ash will not stop looking at where the rider was. The rider rides off at a walk. A tally moment: held or chased by what he does, never scripted (plan tally at the record).
slots.turn: The company knows the hunter is one woman who could have closed and chose not to; Darrow's instinct goes to her first, and the page shows whether he follows it and what that costs.

slots.plan: Her word arrives: a message left where the company must find it (nailed under the writ on a bell-post, or carried by a mill child paid a copper), exact to the point of comedy: the captain of the Ninth is to come to the weir below the mill at first light, alone, under the forms of a knight's meeting, to answer a question; no name signed; the hand a duelist's, every letter cut like a stroke. The company has it out over the fire, loudly, each with a point: Hollis for the forms, Wren for running tonight, Rae for reading the ground first, Maelis for his hands. Ends on the small choice.
slots.turn: Darrow is asked for by the forms, by name and alone, and chooses how a man who swears to no stone answers a knight's summons.

micro.ask: An unsigned summons asks the captain of the Ninth to the weir at first light, alone, under the forms. What does Darrow do?
options: Answer by the forms: go to the weir at the hour named, alone, and let the company watch from the bank.
Owe the forms nothing: take the company to the weir in strength tonight and hold the narrow place before she comes.
Send Wren with his answer and a question of his own: who sent her, and why alive.

slots.plan: The night before the weir. The company reads the ground by lantern: a frozen weir below a mill, the water loud under the ice, one dry stone in the middle where a man can stand square and nobody can come at him from more than one side. Hollis drills him there in the dark, the Seated Blade from his feet: the stance that refuses to move (Stillwater), the sword in the new grip. Rae draws the cart up on the bank where it will do most good and says why. Wren keeps a book on the morning that nobody will bet against. It is rowdy and warm because it has to be, and then it is quiet. Callback c05.7a fits the rowdy part: someone answers for Wren who she is for, in passing, the way the company says true things.
slots.turn: Darrow chooses his ground: the one stone on the weir where footwork is worth nothing and standing is worth everything, and the company arranges itself around that choice.

slots.plan: First light at the weir. She comes alone, on foot, the horse left on the bank, and stops at the ice's edge: courteous, clipped, deadly literal. She asks her question before any blade is drawn: why will he not kneel. He answers, or does not; she tests him once, a single pass on the ice that he survives by refusing to move, and steps back to think about it, which is the strangest thing anyone there has seen a fighter do. She says she has orders to take him alive and does not know why, and that she will take him at the next bell whether he has answered or not. The fight itself waits for the bell: the climax.
slots.turn: Darrow meets the hunter face to face and learns she does not know why he is wanted alive; she learns there is a man her footwork has no answer for.

slots.plan: The hunt from her side, written on the Wednesday or Thursday close: an order to take a man alive with no reason given, and her literal obedience to it; the two carts' tracks out of one, read on the soft ground and believed, and the day lost to the wrong lane; what she is right about (a man who will not be moved has no answer in footwork, and she has never met one); her exactness, funny without her knowing it; the company watched from a distance, each of them weighed. Never why he is wanted alive; nothing of the Spire. Her name is hers in her own head: the interlude may speak it (the reader learns it; the company has only 'the rider'), and the base file takes it from this block. Base file ysra-tal.json and a cast.md entry before the record.
slots.turn: The Needle, who has never disobeyed an order or needed a reason, finds herself wanting one.

world_moves: the reader of writs and his two grey cloaks asked at Coldmere's mill after Thorne's cart and rode on south without it
a levy column drove three farms' cattle and their people east along the river road ahead of it
the first hard frost set the river's weir and shallows in ice, so a cart could cross where there was no bridge

climax.plan: The Weir (arc b2.2). At the bell she comes onto the ice, and the fight is a duel that is almost a conversation: the finest footwork in the Lowmarch against a man standing square on one dry stone who will not be moved and will not kneel (Stillwater Stance, Might). He cannot match her and does not try. By tier: Triumph, he holds until she tires and talks, and she leaves him standing and tells her men he was not there; Hard-won, he holds, Maelis sews him afterward, and she takes a wound she did not expect from a man who did not move; Costly, he holds, but Wren is taken for an hour on the bank and talks her way out, and the hunter now knows the girl's face; Setback, he holds only because Ash takes her blade hand, and she withdraws with the dog's blood on her and a grudge. In every tier she is down on the ice at the end, by his holding or Ash's teeth, and in every tier she says the thing she was told and should not have said: that the Second was told to hold the west bank that morning, and everyone knew the Grace would be thin. Then the choice, with her on the ice.
checks: might (Stillwater Stance: the stone, the stance, refusing to be moved while the best footwork he has ever seen looks for the way round)
resolve (the forms: not chasing her when she gives ground, the one thing that would lose him the stone)
insight (Warden's Eye: reading her orders in her face, and whether she knows why he is wanted alive)
options: Spare her where she lies: have Maelis bind what the ice or Ash has done, and let her men carry her off.
Break her blade hand on the ice and leave her for her men, and take the north road tonight while the hunt has no head.
Let her up with a message for the man who sent her, in Darrow's own words, the ford as he saw it from the water, and watch her walk to her horse.

quest_summary: Confessor Ivo Marrant is coming up the Holloway with five grey cloaks (six in all), a cart, a censer, and a writ naming the Faithless at Saint Ysolde's. Darrow's name is first; Hollis is second. Rae Thorne, the carter who heard the list read, is in the House; her cart and oxen wait at the winch-house below, where one of the six will stay; the rest camp on the lower terrace under the gate.
